prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 12.14. Exact Sanskrit: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः ।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥ १४ ॥ Exact stored meaning: Who is always content, a yogī, self-controlled (yatātmā), of firm conviction (dṛḍha-niścayaḥ), with mind and intellect offered to Me — that devotee of Mine is dear to Me (sa me priyaḥ). Chapter context: Devotion and the qualities of the devotee. Render the precise conduct or quality described: compassion, humility, balance, freedom from possessiveness, or the relevant practice. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: One who harbors no hatred toward any being (adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānām), who is friendly (maitraḥ) and compassionate (karuṇaḥ), free from the sense of 'mine' (nirmamaḥ), free from ego (nirahaṃkāraḥ), equanimous in pain and pleasure (sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ), and forgiving (kṣamī) — Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: One from whom the world is not distressed, and who is not distressed by the world; who is free from joy, envy, fear, and agitation (harṣāmarṣa-bhayodvegaiḥ) — that one is also dear to Me. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene. Phone-first composition update, owner 2026-10-19: phones are the primary reading device, tablets secondary. Keep the complete meaningful scene compact and intelligible at 320–430 logical pixels wide. Arrange the important relationships as one close, coherent central grouping; avoid essential tiny distant figures and wide edge-to-edge action. Keep generous quiet margins on all four sides, no faces, hands, feet, narrative objects or important background subjects touching the frame. The complete square painting will be contained inside the phone reading area, never stretched or cropped to fill it; do not depend on edge cropping. Preserve the approved watercolor style and the exact verse meaning. No labels, letters, sacred syllables, explanatory marks or typography.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.14: Who is always content, a yogī, self-controlled (yatātmā), of firm conviction (dṛḍha-niścayaḥ), with mind and intellect offered to Me — that devotee of Mine is dear to Me (sa me priyaḥ).
